security_spec.violation_condition: The Linux kernel (running as a supervisor domain) implicitly trusts that the RDSM correctly saves and restores msdcfg.SEDA/SETA across domain context switches. If the RDSM violates the normative requirement to 'preserve and restore this configuration state across context switches using secure memory,' one supervisor domain inherits another domain's SEDA/SETA permissions. The kernel has no mechanism to detect or mitigate this—it cannot read back msdcfg to verify, and external debug/trace is transparent to software.
security_spec.summary: RDSM failure to context-switch msdcfg.SEDA/SETA causes cross-domain info leak via inherited external debug/trace permissions; kernel has no visibility into msdcfg and implicitly trusts RDSM correctness

findings.finding: CSR_MSECCFG (0x747) is defined but only the PMM (Pointer Masking) bits are present. No SEDA/SETA bit definitions for external debug/trace access control exist. The Smsdedbga/Smsdetrca extensions are not represented in the kernel's CSR bit definitions.
findings.snippet:
/* mseccfg bits */
#define MSECCFG_PMM                    ENVCFG_PMM
#define MSECCFG_PMM_PMLEN_0            ENVCFG_PMM_PMLEN_0
#define MSECCFG_PMM_PMLEN_7            ENVCFG_PMM_PMLEN_7
#define MSECCFG_PMM_PMLEN_16           ENVCFG_PMM_PMLEN_16

findings.finding: CSR_MSECCFG (0x747) and CSR_MSECCFGH (0x757) address constants are defined but never referenced by any kernel code. No read or write operations to MSECCFG exist anywhere in the kernel, meaning the kernel has no mechanism to check or configure SEDA/SETA bits even if the hardware supported them.

No kernel code, DT bindings, Kconfig options, or any infrastructure exists for the SMSDEDBGA (Supervisor Domain External Debug Access) or SMSDETRCA (Supervisor Domain External Trace Access) RISC-V extensions. The msdcfg register, SEDA/SETA bits, and the RDSM save/restore contract are entirely absent from this kernel tree. The security concern—that the kernel implicitly trusts the RDSM to preserve msdcfg.SEDA/SETA across domain context switches—is moot because the kernel has no awareness of supervisor domains or their debug/trace configuration.
